title: The Solution Doctors Found Too Late
body:
A man in his 60s died after years of using far too much zinc-containing denture cream.

His case was reported in a medical journal in 2010.

The story is real. And the amount of cream involved is a key part of it.

Poison Control describes people using two or more tubes a week, for years. Depending on the product, one tube should have lasted several weeks.

That extreme use meant swallowing much more of the cream than normal.

Doctors saw high zinc and low copper in these patients. They also found nerve damage and too few red blood cells.

Too much zinc can stop the body from getting enough copper. A severe lack of copper can harm both blood cells and nerves.

In the fatal case, the man's nerve damage kept getting worse. The link to his excessive cream use was found late in his illness.

Copper treatment helped his blood problems. His nerve damage did not recover.

The report says he die

I only found out the truth after my stroke, and I wish I'd known it ten years sooner.
